name: Ruy Lopez
desc: White's bishop pressures the knight that guards e5, building slow, long-term pressure. The Closed main line leads to rich manoeuvring battles behind a locked centre.

name: Italian Game
desc: White aims the bishop at f7 and builds quietly with c3 and d3. Both sides castle and manoeuvre before committing in the centre.

name: Sicilian Defense
desc: 5...a6 keeps every option open and prepares ...e5 or ...b5. Against the English Attack the game often becomes a race of opposite-side attacks.

name: Sicilian Defense
desc: Black's g7-bishop rakes the long diagonal. In the Yugoslav Attack White castles long and storms with h4–h5 — one of the sharpest lines in chess.

name: French Defense
desc: Black pins the knight and gives up the dark-squared bishop to double White's pawns. White gets space and the bishop pair; Black gets a solid centre and queenside targets.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
desc: Black develops the light-squared bishop before ...e6, avoiding the French's problem piece. White gains kingside space with h4–h5, but Black's structure stays very solid.

name: Scandinavian Defense
desc: Black challenges e4 at once and recaptures with the queen, which settles on a5. The ...c6 and ...Bf5 setup is compact and easy to learn.

name: Pirc Defense
desc: Black lets White build a big centre, then chips at it with ...c6, ...b5 or ...e5. The Classical System keeps the game calm and positional.

name: Scotch Game
desc: White opens the centre on move 3 for free piece play. In the Mieses line White gains space with e5 and c4 while Black must reroute the d5-knight.

name: Four Knights Game
desc: Both sides develop naturally in a symmetrical, classical structure. Calm and balanced — a good way to learn open-game ideas.

name: Vienna Game
desc: White develops the queen's knight first, then strikes with f4 for a quick kingside initiative. Black's ...d5 hits straight back in the centre.

name: King's Gambit
desc: White gives up the f-pawn for rapid development and an open f-file. The Kieseritzky is a romantic, tactical line where both kings can come under fire.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
desc: Black holds d5 with ...e6 and develops soundly. One of the most reliable replies to 1.d4, though Black must later free the c8-bishop.

name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
desc: Black takes on c4 without trying to keep the pawn, using the time to hit the centre with ...c5. White gets freer development; Black a sound, open position.

name: Slav Defense
desc: ...c6 supports d5 while leaving the c8-bishop free to reach f5. Black grabs c4 briefly, then develops actively with ...Bf5 and ...Bb4.

name: Catalan Opening
desc: White pairs the Queen's Gambit with a g2-fianchetto aimed down the long diagonal. Black takes on c4; White wins the pawn back with lasting queenside pressure.

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
desc: Black pins the c3-knight to fight for e4 with pieces rather than pawns. Sound and flexible, with play revolving around the centre and White's bishop pair.

name: King's Indian Defense
desc: Black concedes the centre, then strikes with ...e5. After d5 the centre locks and both sides attack on opposite wings — Black usually with ...f5.

name: Grünfeld Defense
desc: Black invites White to build a big pawn centre, then attacks it with pieces and ...c5. The Exchange tests whether that centre is a strength or a target.

name: London System
desc: White sets up Bf4, e3, c3 and Nd2 — a solid system that works against almost anything. The plans are easy to learn and rarely go wrong early.

name: English Opening
desc: 1.c4 controls d5 from the flank — a reversed Sicilian with an extra tempo. The g2-bishop keeps steady pressure on the long diagonal.

name: Dutch Defense
desc: 1...f5 grabs e4 and signals kingside ambitions. The Leningrad adds a g7-fianchetto for an unbalanced, fighting game.
